title: Agents' next frontier: agent-to-agent and network effects — Jean-Denis Greze, Town
talk_summary: The talk reframes multi-agent systems as a context-window search problem: the goal is getting the right information into the single LLM call that matters, and agent-to-agent architectures are just ways to approximate access to data across privacy silos. It surveys five strategies (trust-boundary agents, privacy-preserving tools, shared silos/wikis, human-in-the-loop relays, and a 'black box' LLM that reads all silos and only asks permission at the sharing moment), and bets on AI-maintained shared wikis as the near-term ROI winner.

takeaways.what_they_do: An AI inside each private silo holds a policy about what must stay private plus a description of shared spaces, and at end of day sweeps new information into the shared wiki automatically.

takeaways.technique: Shared skills repo as common context
takeaways.what_they_do: Skills live in the repo where anyone can improve them, so one agent's better method (e.g. DB profiling) is reused by every later agent facing the same problem.
takeaways.evidence_quote: If you code in an organization, probably in your repo you have shared skills. Anyone can make them better.

takeaways.what_they_do: Treat every agent run as: ensure the context window right before the tool call contains exactly the right information; everything else is retrieval plumbing.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you're trying to make sure the context window has the right information for the user

takeaways.technique: Low-sensitivity auto zone with LLM policy enforcement
takeaways.what_they_do: Define an explicit low-sensitivity zone where an LLM may decide to share/act without human approval, and let that zone grow as models improve; keep high-sensitivity items human-approved.
takeaways.evidence_quote: definitely define a low sensitivity zone where you're okay with the LLM making a call.

takeaways.technique: Black-box broker with permission only at the sharing step
takeaways.what_they_do: One LLM reads across all silos without per-read approval, narrows to the few owners whose data is actually needed, and asks only them to approve the disclosure/tool call.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it only ask the people who own that information for their approval to do the tool call

takeaways.what_they_do: Warns that one wrong LLM-written fact in a shared wiki persists and poisons future runs (his agent is still called 'Apex' in memory).
takeaways.evidence_quote: one piece of information there is incorrect cuz LLM made a mistake and then it like poisons it forever
